question: After a complete hydatidiform mole, a 26-year-old woman develops gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN). Her WHO/FIGO prognostic score is calculated as 5. Which of the following management plans is most appropriate?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A WHO/FIGO score of ≤6 classifies GTN as low risk. Low-risk GTN is treated with single-agent chemotherapy (methotrexate or actinomycin-D), achieving cure rates >95%. Multi-agent regimens are reserved for high-risk disease (score ≥7).

Incorrect. EMA-CO (etoposide, methotrexate, actinomycin-D, cyclophosphamide, vincristine) is reserved for high-risk GTN, defined by WHO/FIGO score ≥7. This patient's score of 5 places her in the low-risk category.

answers.text: Immediate hysterectomy because she has already completed her family

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. GTN is exquisitely chemosensitive. Even in patients who have completed their family, hysterectomy is not recommended as first-line treatment for GTN because chemotherapy achieves >95% cure. Hysterectomy may be considered in selected refractory cases.

answers.text: Serial β-hCG monitoring without chemotherapy for 3 months

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Once GTN is diagnosed (based on rising or plateaued β-hCG meeting WHO criteria), chemotherapy should begin promptly. Watchful waiting risks disease progression and loss of curability.

overallFeedback.feedback: WHO/FIGO prognostic score ≤6 = low risk = single-agent chemo. Score ≥7 = high risk = multi-agent EMA-CO.
Correct. WHO/FIGO score ≤6 = low-risk GTN → single-agent chemotherapy (methotrexate or actinomycin-D).
